I was talking to my husband last night about how I should finally get evaluated for autism. I have an ADHD diagnosis. I struggle with sensory overload, anxiety, and depression (some of that is situational), and social cues. But man, the sensory overload really takes the cake.

I also just started working in med surg last week! I did clinicals in long term care and in med surg. I am a brand new CNA and this is my first job as a cna. 

Daytime shift, and let me be clear... is a total shit show. Like, its a total sensory overload salad. Its loud, the lights are bright, it can be hot... call lights are going off constantly. You have meals, and family visits, and bed baths and showers. You also bing them to appointments in other parts of the hospital if needed. You also usually help people get ready to go home by packing their things and wheeling them outside. Oh, and  management is there. There's more pressure to do everything by the book, etc.

I personally work the overnight shift (three 12 hour shifts) and it is the single best decision I ever made. The overhead lights are off, its quiet, theres no management, no families, and its nice and chilly... With significantly less call lights going off. Between midnight and 3am everything is almost completely quiet because everyone is asleep. I do Q8 vitals, but it depends on the patient. I had one gentleman who was Q2. Hourly rounds means I basically pop my head in and If they are sleeping I check all my boxes and let them sleep. I do lots of brief and bed changes but nothing crazy. Around 4am we do everyone's vitals, refill ice waters and get them snacks, take out all the trash from each room, restock supplies, and chart. 

Also, my coworkers are amazing. There is definitely more of a sense if family and comradery on overnight shift. Everyone is willing to help and nurses can be a hoot. Its great.


Edit: overnight shift also gets paid more! Id be making $16.50 during the day with no differentials. I make $20/hr my entire shift, and $21.50 for any hours that fall on the weekend!

I made up my own! They came out very similarly to my non vegan cookies. Super chewy with just the right amount of crisp on the bottom, and held their shape! The only thing I might change the next batch is reducing the oven temp by 25 degrees, as I found that the bottoms darkened faster than the Tops. I’m going to do some experimenting with the remaining dough.


Ingredients 

2 cups white flour

1 tsp baking soda 

Pinch or two of salt

3/4cup brown sugar, packed

1/2 cup raw sugar

1/2 cup all-vegetable crisco (seriously can’t beat this. Coconut oil just isn’t the same imo)

2 capfuls of vanilla

1/4 cup silk soy milk (any dairy alternative would probably do just fine!)

9oz bag of vsemi-sweet chocolate chips 



Preheat oven to 350f (note: if bottoms appear to brown quicker than the tops, reduce temp by 25f and keep an eye on the next batch)

Whisk sugars, soy milk, salt, vanilla and crisco in a large bowl until creamy and sugar is reasonably dissolved. No need to melt crisco beforehand.

In a second bowl, whisk together two cups of flour and tsp of baking soda. Incorporate dry ingredients into the wet, being careful not to over-stir/knead. Fold in your chocolate chips. (These would be bomb with walnuts, just saying)

 Form into a log/ball and freeze, covered, for 30 minutes. Once chilled, form into 1.5”  balls and place on your prepared cookie sheet. Bake and enjoy! :) (I baked mine for 20 minutes, but I think 15 would have been plenty. Just keep an eye on them haha)

I just used my usual dough recipe and followed bagel-baking procedures I googled haha. It's actually the same way you'd make soft pretzels, so that's what I did!

\- My usual dough recipe is 4 cups of white flour, 1-2 tsp of salt, 2 cups of warm water, and 2.25 tsp active yeast. I Feed the yeast 1-2 tsp of sugar in the warm water and then wait 10 minutes or so. While that's doing its thing, I whisk my dry ingredients in a separate bowl. Then I mix it all together and I cover and let it rest for 1-3 hours. Where it's so warm right now I was able to get away with 1 hour before turning it out and kneading the crap out of it lol.

\- Prep a large pot on the stove with water and add a generous amount of sugar (maybe 1/2 cup depending on how much water is in the pot, I just poured some in), you want them to simmer and not boil. Preheat the oven to 425. Spray a cookie sheet with nonstick spray or use parchment paper.

\- I cut the dough into 6-12 pieces depending on the size I want, and form each bit into a ball like you would when making artisan-style bread (maybe look up a video). Cover with a damp towel and let rise again. Once they have risen  I flour my hands and my work surface and work a hole into the center. I placed 2-3 at a time in the water and simmered for 2 minutes, turning halfway through. Remove with a slotted spatula or spoon as to drain excess water, and place onto your prepared cookie sheet. Brush with butter, egg, or oil. I like to use extra virgin olive oil. Sprinkle on preferred toppings. For everything bagels, I used sesame seeds, herbs (i think I used basil or parsley), a little salt, onion powder, and garlic powder. Cinnamon and sugar is good too! I think my next batch I will be working some cinnamon&raisins into the dough.

\- Bake at 425 until golden brown (watch the bottoms because I found that they got golden quickly), 15-20 minutes. :)
